h1:
Paknam & Bang Pu Seafood
8 Seaside Spots Bangkokers Drive Out For
intro: Paknam and Bang Pu are about as close to the sea as you can get from Bangkok — under an hour from the city and you're sitting in the sea breeze eating fresh prawns, shellfish, crab and fish. These are the 8 spots Bangkokers actually drive out for, picked from real reviews and places open right now, from a Michelin Guide restaurant to old-school riverside joints that won't dent your wallet.
chips: 🚗 Close to Bangkok, easy day trip

blocks.html: Samut Prakan sits right on the Gulf of Thailand, which is why locals nickname it Mueang Paknam ("river-mouth town"). The seafood here is fresh and reaches the kitchen fast — no long haul. The main seafood areas split into two zones: the Paknam area in town (reachable via BTS Paknam) and Bang Pu, out along Sukhumvit Road toward Samut Sakhon, a strip of genuinely seaside restaurants where you catch the real breeze. If you want somewhere quieter, cross over to the Phra Chulachomklao Fort area at Laem Fa Pha.

We ranked these on three things combined: how fresh the ingredients are, the seaside or riverside setting, and value for the price. The prices listed are averages per person or per dish as stated by the restaurants and reviews. Anything sold by weight (especially crab and giant river prawns) you should always price per kilo before ordering, since it rises and falls with the season.

blocks.text: Ranking the seafood spots in Paknam & Bang Pu

items.name: Rabieng Talay Bang Pu
items.blurb: A seaside spot in Bang Pu that's been in the Michelin Guide for several years running. The tables really do sit right by the water, the breeze is cool, and in the evening you catch the sunset. The dish on nearly every table is the sour curry with snapper roe (kaeng som) — a rounded, tangy broth — alongside the sweet, fresh raw prawns in fish sauce. Plenty of Bangkokers drive out here specifically for it. It gets very busy on weekends, so call to book or arrive before the peak.

items.name: Moken Bang Pu
items.blurb: A seaside restaurant in Soi Bang Pu 126/2 off Sukhumvit Road, open since 2017 and named after the Moken sea-gypsy people. The setting is relaxed, with both an air-conditioned zone and open-air tables in the sea breeze. The dishes people talk about are the shrimp-paste miang, shrimp-paste omelette, grilled giant river prawns and blue crab in curry powder. Steamed crab is priced per piece (around 900 THB each depending on size). Toward evening a flock of seagulls flies in for the show. Book ahead on weekends.

items.name: Sompong Seafood
items.blurb: An old-timer of more than 20 years that once earned the Samut Prakan provincial quality seal. It's a big garden restaurant with both air-conditioned rooms and outdoor seating, and you can order small or large plates depending on your group size. Frequent orders include the steamed crab claw meat, grilled giant river prawns, steamed grouper with soy sauce, and stir-fried Hong Kong kale over high heat. Good for bringing the whole family for a proper table. Some reviews note the cooking runs a touch sweet — if that's not your thing, ask them to ease off.

items.name: Rim Khuean Seafood (the old one)
items.blurb: A long-running seafood joint in central Paknam, near Soi Dabphloeng across from the city observation tower. You sit at open-air tables by the embankment, unpretentious and down-to-earth — good for meeting friends over an evening meal. People order the prawns in fish sauce, baked prawns with glass noodles, steamed blue crab, horseshoe crab egg salad and blue-crab papaya salad. Prices are lighter than the seaside spots in Bang Pu, and it's easy to reach since it's near BTS Paknam.

items.name: Phra Chula Fort Club Seafood by Ja Pui
items.blurb: Set inside the Phra Chulachomklao Fort grounds at Laem Fa Pha, on the Phra Samut Chedi side. The setting is quiet and canalside, surrounded by the army's protected forest, with a cool afternoon breeze and a boat pier next to the restaurant. Standout dishes lean toward pickled bamboo-shoot sour curry with sea catfish, crab fried rice, seafood tom yum and squid stir-fried with salted egg. You'll pass an army checkpoint and need to show ID. Good for anyone wanting a setting unlike the usual seaside spots, and you can pair it with a visit to the fort on the same trip.
items.meta: Laem Fa Pha, Phra Chula Fort · 10:00–21:00

items.name: Baan Chidlom Bang Pu
items.blurb: A Bang Pu seafood restaurant with a riverside setting, good for a special meal or a long, leisurely family lunch. Recommended dishes are the shrimp cakes, deep-fried sea bass with herbs, crab in curry powder and grilled river prawns. The plating is pretty, and it's a comfortable choice that isn't as crowded as the famous spots.

items.name: Lung Waen Seafood
items.blurb: A fresh riverside seafood spot with prices you can actually reach — dishes run from around 70 THB up to 500 THB. People often order the crab in curry powder, stir-fried soft-shell crab and grilled river prawns. Good for anyone who wants fresh seafood without paying a fortune; order a few things to share and keep the bill under control.

items.name: Krua Hua Ko Kin Lom Chom Le
items.blurb: A riverside spot near Bang Khlong Market in Mueang district, where you sit watching the boats pass by at an easy pace. The focus is home-style fresh seafood at local prices. Good for anyone after a genuinely local place that isn't about photos — just fresh ingredients at a fair price.

blocks.title: Tips for ordering seafood that's worth it
blocks.html: Crab and giant river prawns are charged by weight, and prices swing with the season — once you order, ask the price per kilo and ask to see the actual piece before it's weighed to be sure. Shellfish (cockles, blanched clams, oysters) are the value play that many places do well — order some to nibble before the heavy dishes so you don't fill up too fast.

blocks.text: Paknam or Bang Pu — which zone should you pick?

blocks.html: If you want a real sea view, strong breeze and sunset, head to the Bang Pu zone — spots like Rabieng Talay and Moken sit right by the water, and you can linger from afternoon into the evening. But if you'd rather have somewhere easy to reach, light on the wallet and no booking needed, the Paknam area in town does the job better, especially the embankment spots near BTS Paknam — hop off the train and grab a motorbike taxi straight there.

items.name: Bang Pu zone
items.blurb: Genuine seaside breeze and a sunset view. The famous spots need a weekend booking — best for a long, leisurely special meal.

items.name: Paknam zone (in town)
items.blurb: Easy to reach, near BTS Paknam, with old-school spots that are light on the wallet — good for an unplanned evening meal.

items.name: Phra Chula Fort / Laem Fa Pha zone
items.blurb: Quiet and canalside, over on the Phra Samut Chedi side — pair a meal with a visit to the old fort on the same trip.

blocks.text: Seafood dishes not to miss around here

items: Raw prawns in fish sauce — fresh prawns under a sharp, zingy seafood dipping sauce, the table-opener almost every place has. Rabieng Talay and Rim Khuean both do it well.
Sour curry with fish roe — a tangy sour curry with fish roe (snapper/rivulated roe), the signature dish of the Bang Pu spots, eaten with hot steamed rice.
Steamed blue crab / steamed crab claw meat — fresh crab steamed and served with seafood dipping sauce, priced per piece or per kilo, so ask before ordering.
Grilled giant river prawns — big prawns oozing with roe, grilled and dipped in seafood sauce, the star of many menus.
Blanched clams / loaded oysters — good-value shellfish dishes to nibble while you wait for the mains.

blocks.text: How to drive out from Bangkok, and do you need to book?

blocks.html: From Bangkok, drive to Paknam via Sukhumvit Road or take the expressway and exit at Paknam — about 40 minutes to an hour depending on where you start and the traffic. For Bang Pu, keep going along Sukhumvit a bit farther toward Samut Sakhon. If you're not driving, take the BTS Green Line to Paknam station, then grab a motorbike taxi or taxi to the in-town spots.

The famous seaside spots like Rabieng Talay and Moken fill up fast on Saturdays, Sundays and long weekends — call ahead to book or arrive before the peak (around noon and 5 pm). Most of the in-town Paknam spots take walk-ins, though fresh seafood means some dishes sell out toward the end of service. If you've got your heart set on something specific, go early in the service window for the fullest choice.

faq.q: Which seafood restaurant in Paknam–Bang Pu is the best?
faq.a: Going by reviews and its Michelin Guide listing, Rabieng Talay Bang Pu is right up at the top, since it's genuinely seaside and the seafood is fresh. The standout dishes are the sour curry with snapper roe and the raw prawns in fish sauce. But if you want lighter prices and an easy trip, Rim Khuean Seafood in central Paknam is an old-school favorite people keep going back to.

faq.q: Which zone should I pick for a real sea view?
faq.a: Head to the Bang Pu zone along Sukhumvit Road — spots like Rabieng Talay and Moken have tables right by the water, catching the breeze and the sunset. The Paknam area in town is more embankment and riverside than wide-open sea view.

faq.q: How long is the drive from Bangkok, and do I need to book?
faq.a: It's about 40 minutes to an hour from Bangkok to Paknam depending on where you start and traffic, then a bit farther for Bang Pu. The famous seaside spots get busy on weekends, so call to book or arrive before noon and 5 pm. Most in-town spots take walk-ins.

In-town Paknam spots like Rim Khuean average around 300 THB per person; the Bang Pu seaside spots like Rabieng Talay and Moken average around 250–500 THB per person. Note that crab and giant river prawns are charged by weight, so ask the price per kilo before ordering.

faq.q: Can I get there without my own car?
faq.a: Yes — take the BTS Green Line to Paknam station, then a motorbike taxi or taxi to the in-town spots like Rim Khuean Seafood is easy. The Bang Pu and Phra Chula Fort zones are farther from the station and suit those with a car better.
